text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The prosecutor's office officially charged deputy Valdis Krisbergs with fraud and falsification of bookkeeping records.
- Parliament turned down the request of President Guntis Ulmanis to alter the law on lotteries and gambling, which now prohibits gambling businesses to operate in basements.

- Delegations of Latvia and Lithuania met in Vilnius in yet another attempt to solve the long-standing conflict over the maritime border dispute between the two countries. They agreed the border issue and that of potential oil fields should be considered separately.
- Economy Minister Guntar Krasts believes that his influence on the privatisation process in Latvia was close to zero and that business has started to merge dangerously with politics.

- Defence Minister Andrejs Krastinsh announced while meeting with his Ukrainian counterpart in Kiev that Latvia would sign individual treaties with each of the NATO members and would become a full-fledged member of the alliance by the end of this year. He also pledged to support the Ukraine in its efforts to join the bloc.
- After auditing Riga Aviation University the state audit suggests that its chancellor should be dismissed.
- Riga Shipyard reported a 235,000 lat net profit in 1996 and paid 2.6 million lats in taxes to the state budget. The plant's turnover was up from seven million lats to 12.2 million lats.
- The government gave conceptual approval to a proposal by the ministry of agriculture to increase by 4.6 million lats the amount of subsidies to agriculture.
- At this week's cabinet meeting, the government reviewed its stand on talks with the WTO.
